'''''Berula erecta''''', known as '''lesser water-parsnip''', '''cutleaf waterparsnip''', or '''narrow-leaved water-parsnip''',<ref name=jacqui/> is a member of the [[Apiaceae|carrot family]]. Growing to around {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on|0}} tall, it is found in or by water.<ref>{{Citation |last=Stace |first=Clive |author-link = Clive Stace |year=2010b |title=New Flora of the British Isles |edition=3rd |location=Cambridge, UK |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 |page=814 }}</ref> It is widespread across much of [[Europe]], [[Asia]], [[Australia]], and [[North America]].<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Berula%20erecta.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref name=jacqui>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=berula+erecta Altervista Flora Italiana, Sedanina d'acqua, Cutleaf Waterparsnip, ''Berula erecta'' (Huds.) Coville]</ref><ref name=wilma>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200015407 Flora of China, <big>天山泽芹</big> tian shan ze qin ''Berula erecta'' (Hudson) Coville, Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 4: 115. 1893. ]</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/Berula+erecta Atlas of Living Australia]</ref>

''Berula erecta'' has a hollow stem. Underwater leaves consist of compound with thread-like lobes; leaves above the surface of the water are flatter and broader. The  plant produces many small white flowers in a compound [[umbel]].<ref name=wilma/>

== Description ==
''Berula erecta'' occurs on poorly drained neutral and acidic soils of the lowlands and upland fringe. It is found in the South West of England, especially in [[Devon]]. It typically resides in shallow aquatic environments containing moderate nutrient levels.<ref name=":0" /> During the winter, its stem and body become completely submerged underwater. ''Berula erecta'' has been shown to survive and grow better after living in stressful conditions with either limiting or excess nutrients or mechanical stress.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Milliken|first=W.|date=1999|title=Native American Ethnobotany. Daniel E. Moerman. Portland, Oregon: Timber Press. 1998. 927pp. ISBN 0 88192 453 9. US$ 79.95 (hardback).|journal=Edinburgh Journal of Botany|volume=56|issue=2|pages=317–318|doi=10.1017/s0960428600001244|issn=0960-4286|doi-access=free}}</ref>

''Berula erecta'' has toothed leaves from one and a half to two inches across, each containing around twenty white flowers. The plant can grow from around one to three feet tall.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.minnesotawildflowers.info/flower/cut-leaf-water-parsnip|title=Berula erecta (Cut-leaf Water Parsnip): Minnesota Wildflowers|website=www.minnesotawildflowers.info|language=en|access-date=2018-12-04}}</ref> The stalk has a pale ring at its base that makes the plant distinguishable, and has a scent of carrot or parsnip when crushed.<ref name=":2">{{citation |mode=cs1 |title=information-sheet-information-sheet-feb-1994-18-pp|doi = 10.1163/2210-7975_hrd-2338-0059}}</ref>

The natural communities for ''Berula erecta'' are as listed:<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://mnfi.anr.msu.edu/species/description/13319/Berula-erecta|title=Berula erecta (Cut-leaved water parsnip) - Michigan Natural Features Inventory|date=n.d.|website=mnfi.anr.msu.edu|access-date=2018-12-04}}</ref>

* Emergent marsh
* Floodplain forest
* Hardwood-conifer swamp
* Headwater stream (1st-2nd order), riffle
* Headwater stream (1st-2nd order), pool
* Headwater stream (1st-2nd order), run
* Prairie fen
* Rich conifer swamp
* Rich tamarack swamp
* Southern shrub-carr
* Southern [[wet meadow]]

==Uses==
The [[Zuni people]] use ''Berula erecta'' as an ingredient of "schumaakwe cakes" and used it externally for rheumatism.<ref>Stevenson, Matilda Coxe 1915 Ethnobotany of the Zuni Indians. SI-BAE Annual Report #30 (p.44)</ref> An infusion of the whole plant is used as wash for rashes and athlete's foot infection.<ref>Camazine, Scott and Robert A. Bye 1980 A Study Of The Medical Ethnobotany Of The Zuni Indians of New Mexico. Journal of Ethnopharmacology 2:365-388(p.379)</ref>

Some [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native American]] peoples have been known to use ''Berula erecta'' for medicinal purposes.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

''Berula erecta'' has been studied for its [[essential oil]] that has been believed to possibly have medicinal uses.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Lazarević|first1=Jelena|last2=Radulović|first2=Niko|last3=Palić|first3=Radosav|last4=Zlatković|first4=Bojan|date=2010|title=Chemical Analysis of Volatile Constituents ofBerula erecta(Hudson) Coville subsp.erecta(Apiaceae) From Serbia|journal=Journal of Essential Oil Research|language=en|volume=22|issue=2|pages=153–156|doi=10.1080/10412905.2010.9700290|s2cid=95697964|issn=1041-2905}}</ref> The plant's essential oil has been shown to contain [[polyacetylene]]s. Polyacetylenes have a wide range of beneficial medicinal effects. One is its nematodicidal effects that could potentially be beneficial in agriculture<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Chitwood|first=David J.|title=Phytochemicalbasedstrategies Fornematodecontrol|date=2002|journal=Annual Review of Phytopathology|volume=40|issue=1|pages=221–249|doi=10.1146/annurev.phyto.40.032602.130045|pmid=12147760|issn=0066-4286}}</ref> as well its positive effects on human health.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brandt|first1=K|last2=Christensen|first2=L.P|last3=Hansen-Møller|first3=J|last4=Hansen|first4=S.L|last5=Haraldsdottir|first5=J|last6=Jespersen|first6=L|last7=Purup|first7=S|last8=Kharazmi|first8=A|last9=Barkholt|first9=V|date=2004|title=Health promoting compounds in vegetables and fruits|journal=Trends in Food Science & Technology|volume=15|issue=7–8|pages=384–393|doi=10.1016/j.tifs.2003.12.003|issn=0924-2244}}</ref> Polyacetylenes also are [[antifungal]], [[antibacterial]], and have [[antiallergenic]] and anti-inflammatory properties.<ref name=":0" />

However, medicinal use of pure polyacetylenes is not feasible due to their high chemical instability as well as a tendency to evoke allergic reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hausen|first1=B. M.|last2=Bröhas|first2=J.|last3=König|first3=W. A.|last4=Faasch|first4=H.|last5=Hahn|first5=H.|last6=Bruhn|first6=G.|date=1987|title=Allergic and irritant contact dermatitis from falcarinol and didehydrofalcarinol in common ivy (Hedera helixL.)|journal=Contact Dermatitis|volume=17|issue=1|pages=1–9|doi=10.1111/j.1600-0536.1987.tb02634.x|pmid=3652685|s2cid=38387422|issn=0105-1873}}</ref> For this reason, consuming smaller and less pure amounts of polyacetylenes from the essential oil of ''Berula erecta'' may be viable.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hansen|first1=Susanne L|last2=Purup|first2=Stig|last3=Christensen|first3=Lars P|date=2003|title=Bioactivity of falcarinol and the influenceof processing and storage on its content in carrots (Daucus carota L)|journal=Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture|volume=83|issue=10|pages=1010–1017|doi=10.1002/jsfa.1442|bibcode=2003JSFA...83.1010H |issn=0022-5142}}</ref>

Following the first cut of the season, ''Berula erecta'' will likely regrow and produce flowers several times again in the same growing season.<ref name=":2" />

==Conservation==
''Berula erecta'' (lesser water parsnip) is a component of  [[Purple moor grass and rush pastures]] - a type of [[Biodiversity Action Plan habitat]] in the UK.{{Cn|date=May 2021}}

The species is globally classified as a [[least-concern species]], but is a [[threatened species]] in the United States.<ref name=":3" /> In Estonia, it is a [[near-threatened species]] and an [[endangered species]] in [[Norway]].<ref name=IUCN/>

The species is threatened by invasive [[wetland]] species such as [[watercress]] that can quickly destroy its habitat.<ref name=":1" />

Recommended steps to promote conservation of ''Berula erecta'' are keeping an open canopy for the species as well as maintenance of groundwater sources that may include periodic controlled burns.<ref name=":3" />
